newsitem.title: USA: Parents press again for American Berenson's freedom.
newsitem.headline: Parents press again for American Berenson's freedom.

text.p: With the end of the hostage drama in Lima, the parents of a New Yorker jailed for life in Peru as a Tupac Amaru guerrilla broke their silence on Sunday to press again for her freedom.

"For 4-1/2 months, we've refrained from speaking on behalf of our daughter Lori because of the human aspects of the hostage crisis ... and our overwhelming concern for the captives," her father, Mark Berenson, told Reuters.

"Now that this crisis has been resolved we must press openly once again for a fair trial in a civilian court so she can prove her innocence and come home," he said. "She has been wrongfully incarcerated for 524 days."
The Clinton administration has repeatedly called for a non-military trial for Lori Berenson, a 27-year-old from Manhattan's Gramercy Park district.

Berenson was sentenced in January 1996 by a secret "faceless" military court for treason and being a leader of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), the force that held the Japanese ambassador's residence for 126 days.
The siege ended last Tuesday when commandos swarmed into the house through secret tunnels, killing all 14 MRTA captors and rescuing all but one of the 72 hostages.

Berenson was among 20 people whose freedom the Tupac Amaru guerrillas demanded in the final stretch of their negotiations with the government, the opposition La Republica and pro-government Expreso dailies reported. The guerrillas had originally sought freedom for 450 imprisoned rebels.
Citing a hostage source, Expreso said on Sunday the rebels called for her release as a way of winning over American public opinion to the MRTA.

Mark Berenson said his daughter never knew longtime MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa, the siege commander whose bullet-ridden corpse was seen on TV after the raid sprawled on a staircase in the gutted and bombed-out house.
"I don't think she knew any of the people involved (in the hostage takeover)," Mr. Berenson said. "Why would she, she was arrested over a year ago and jailed over 500 miles (800 km) away?"

During an interrogation by a military judge after her November 1995 arrest, Lori denied she had ever met Cerpa, even when prodded to acknowledge she knew someone who fit his physical description, her family's U.S.-based lawyer, Tom Nooter, told Reuters on Sunday.

Berenson has expressed sympathy for the MRTA, but rejects charges of participation in guerrilla activity. She seeks to prove her innocence by producing evidence and having a lawyer confront witnesses, her parents say.
Backing her demand for an open trial are President Bill Clinton, 107 members of Congress and former U.S. President Jimmy Carter.
"It is time for Peru to demonstrate that they are strongly committed to human rights and due process in particular and to give Lori a fair trail in civilian court," Mark Berenson said.
